conventions.convention: Geometry is smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable and boundaryless, with Lorentz signature (−,+,+,+), a time orientation and an independently supplied manifold orientation. The connection is torsion-free and metric-compatible.
Physical local potentials are A_i=κ₀a_i, with A_j=A_i+κ₀df_ij and physical curvature F=dA_i. Fixed-sector physical connection variations are global real one-forms α and satisfy δF=dα.
The sourced equation is ∇ₐFᵃᵇ=−μ₀jᵇ, equivalently d(⋆F)=μ₀ι_j vol_g. Matter current is normalized by δ_A S_m=c⁻¹∫jᵃαₐ vol_g, and inverse-metric stress by δ_g S_m=−(2c)⁻¹∫T_ab qᵃᵇ vol_g.
Charged representatives satisfy φ_j=g_ij^k φ_i, Dₐφ=∂ₐφ−iλAₐφ and λκ₀=k∈ℤ in the circle-bundle branch. The separate global real-potential branch permits arbitrary real λ.

Metric variations are smooth families fixed outside a common compact set for sufficiently small parameters. Divergent background actions are handled through compactly supported action differences. Einstein–Hilbert normalization is c³/(16πG_N), giving κ_E=8πG_N/c⁴.
The boundary example integrates over H={x³≥0} inside boundaryless ambient ℝ⁴, with outward conormal −dx³. Its variation fixes boundary metric values but permits nonzero normal derivatives.

Countable Choice is inherited from the geometric suppliers; no full Axiom of Choice or additional infinite selection is claimed by the local calculations. SI assignments are formal dimensional bookkeeping, with no measured inputs or empirical conclusions.

load_bearing.statement: On the stated smooth oriented Lorentzian geometry and fixed bundle sector, define Pₐ=∂ₐφ−iλAₐφ, L_φ=gᵃᵇ conjugate(Pₐ)P_b+V(|φ|²), and S_φ=−K_φ(2c)⁻¹∫L_φ vol_g, using compact differences when necessary. Here K_φ>0, V is real and smooth on an open neighborhood of the attained range, and λκ₀=k∈ℤ in the circle branch; the separate global real-potential branch permits real λ.

For the defined smooth scalar functional and compact fixed-sector variations, E_φ=DₐPᵃ−V'(|φ|²)φ, jᵃ=K_φλ Im(conjugate(φ)Pᵃ), and T^φ_ab=K_φ Re(conjugate(Pₐ)P_b)−(K_φ/2)g_ab L_φ give the stated three first variations. Scalar stationarity is equivalent to E_φ=0. Off shell, ∇ₐjᵃ=K_φλ Im(conjugate(φ)E_φ) and ∇ₐ(T^φ)ᵃ_b=K_φ Re(conjugate(E_φ)P_b)+F_ba jᵃ.

For the stated smooth Lorentzian principal-circle-bundle configuration, assume matter stationarity, the displayed Hilbert/current first variation, compact gauge invariance and invariance under simultaneous horizontal-lifted flow transport. Then ∇ₐjᵃ=0 and ∇ₐT_mᵃᵇ=Fᵇᶜj_c, without assuming Maxwell or Einstein equations.

For the stated smooth geometry, fixed connection and matter fields, positive c,G_N,μ₀, constant Λ and compact metric variations, δS_tot=[c³/(16πG_N)]∫[G_ab+Λg_ab−κ_E(T^EM_ab+T^m_ab)]qᵃᵇ vol_g. Stationarity under every such variation is equivalent to the displayed Einstein equation, which necessarily implies vanishing total-stress divergence.
For smooth F and j on the stated oriented Lorentzian open domain, μ₀>0, dF=0 and ∇ₐFᵃᵇ=−μ₀jᵇ, the tensor T^EM_ab=μ₀⁻¹(F_ac F_b{}ᶜ−g_ab F_cd Fᶜᵈ/4) satisfies ∇ₐT_EMᵃᵇ=−Fᵇᶜj_c.

concerns.concern: The Statement introduces “a smooth matter configuration” and “a real differentiable functional of (g,A,Ψ)” without specifying the configuration space, admissible matter directions or meaning of differentiability and induced transport on that space. The displayed first-variation and invariance assumptions support the calculation, but the abstract matter interface needs an explicit definition to meet the workspace's definition requirement.

Step 3.1 says “thus the general identity [F4] applies,” while the scalar Definition permits only relative compact action differences when the global action diverges, and the cited Noether lemma states a real differentiable functional. Explain the relative-action extension or restrict this auxiliary application to finite actions. The independent off-shell calculation in steps 2.1–2.2 already establishes the claimed balances.
